definition: Truth as a substantive property: a sentence is true when it represents things as they are, and only sentences that state how things are (truth-apt sentences) can be true. O'Connor's 'no truth value: not the kind of sentence that can be true or false' denies moral statements truth in this sense; `Holds` in the emotivism results is truth in this sense.
note: The robust/minimal contrast is the project's label from the debate on truth minimalism (Horwich, Wright, Blackburn); no witness of that debate is pinned. The sourced content it labels is O'Connor's gloss (claim OCONNOR-DESTINY-ETHICS-NOT-TRUE-OR-FALSE).
